Congenital cardiac malformation defines this umbrella; extracardiac anomalies vary across syndromes without a shared additional organ.
Inherited neutrophil deficiency is both a blood-cell disorder and an innate immunodeficiency; secondary infections do not establish additional organ involvement.
Corticospinal dysfunction causes spastic weakness and gait impairment; skeletal deformities occur in only 1/5 and weakness alone does not establish muscle disease.

Shared defining phenotype is syndromic neurodevelopmental disability; gastrointestinal, ocular and other manifestations vary across Pitt-Hopkins and Pitt-Hopkins-like subtypes.

Skeletal defects, cutis laxa and developmental disability define syndrome; strabismus/ptosis occur in 30-79%. Dental defects and hepatic adenoma omitted at cap; very small case series.
Inherited oxysterol metabolism disorder; neurologic spastic paraplegia and hepatic bile-acid disease are subtype-specific, without established shared organ frequencies.
Secondary elevation of blood platelets defines the condition; an underlying infection or inflammatory disease is separate and does not make thrombocytosis an immune disorder.
Permanent digital contractures and abnormal taurine/amino-acid excretion define the syndrome; aminoaciduria alone does not establish renal injury.

Severe periodontal destruction, skin fragility and joint hypermobility define this EDS subtype. Arterial dissection is 1-4%; varicose veins are separately diagnosed.
ZC4H2-associated spectrum combines congenital arthrogryposis and muscle abnormalities with motor and neurodevelopmental impairment.
Malaria-associated massive intravascular hemolysis; hemoglobin-mediated acute kidney injury is a common severe manifestation, affecting approximately 30% or more in reported series.
